Physiology + সরল ও দ্বিপদী সমীকরণ এবং অস.question: ১) Saltatory conduction occurs in....... nerve fiber?
Physiology + সরল ও দ্বিপদী সমীকরণ এবং অস.exp:
Saltatory conduction occurs in myelinated nerve fibers. The myelin sheath electrically insulates the axon, so the action potential effectively “jumps” from one node of Ranvier to the next, greatly increasing conduction velocity

Other options:

  • Demyelinated: Saltatory conduction is lost; conduction becomes slow and may fail.

  • Partially myelinated: Not the standard answer; saltatory conduction requires appropriately myelinated axonal segments with nodes.

  • All of them: Incorrect because demyelinated fibers do not exhibit normal saltatory conduction.

High-yield Neurophysiology recall:
Myelinated fiber → saltatory conduction → node of Ranvier → faster conduction.

Exam pearl:
Saltatory = “jumping” from node to node in a myelinated axon.

Physiology + সরল ও দ্বিপদী সমীকরণ এবং অস.question: ২) How many types of neuron are there according to functions?
Physiology + সরল ও দ্বিপদী সমীকরণ এবং অস.exp:
According to function, neurons are classified into 3 types:

  1. Sensory (afferent) neurons — carry impulses from receptors to the CNS.

  2. Motor (efferent) neurons — carry impulses from the CNS to muscles or glands.

  3. Interneurons (association neurons) — connect neurons within the CNS and integrate information.

Other options:

  • 2: Incomplete; sensory and motor neurons alone do not include interneurons.

  • 4 / 5: Not the standard functional classification.

High-yield Neuroanatomy recall:
Functional classification = sensory + motor + interneuron = 3 types.

Exam pearl:
Functionally, neurons are always classically divided into 3 types.

Physiology + সরল ও দ্বিপদী সমীকরণ এবং অস.question: ৩) When a nerve is stimulated by a stimulus it gives maximum response or does not give response at all. - this phenomenon is called?
Physiology + সরল ও দ্বিপদী সমীকরণ এবং অস.exp:
The all-or-none law states that when a nerve fiber is stimulated with a stimulus reaching the threshold, it produces a maximal action potential; if the stimulus is below threshold, there is no action potential.

Thus, the response is essentially maximum or absent, rather than graded.

Other options:

  • Summation: Addition of individual stimuli to produce a greater response.

  • Accommodation: Reduced excitability of a nerve to a slowly rising stimulus.

  • Indefatigability: Refers to the relative resistance of nerve fibers to fatigue.

High-yield Neurophysiology recall:
Threshold stimulus → full action potential; subthreshold stimulus → no action potential.

Exam pearl:
“All or none” = either full response or no response.

Physiology + সরল ও দ্বিপদী সমীকরণ এবং অস.question: ৪) Which of the following is not a properties of nerve fibers?
Physiology + সরল ও দ্বিপদী সমীকরণ এবং অস.exp:
Contractility is a characteristic property of muscle fibers, not nerve fibers. Nerve fibers are capable of responding to stimuli by generating and conducting electrical impulses.

Important properties of nerve fibers include excitability, conductivity, adaptation, and accommodation.

Other options:

  • Excitability: Ability to respond to an adequate stimulus by generating an action potential.

  • Adaptation: Decreased response to a sustained stimulus.

  • Accommodation: Reduced excitability when a stimulus increases slowly.

High-yield Neurophysiology recall:
Nerve → excitability + conductivity
Muscle → excitability + contractility

Exam pearl:
Contractility = muscle property, not a ne

Physiology + সরল ও দ্বিপদী সমীকরণ এবং অস.question: ৫) Wallerian degeneration is the pathological change that occurs in the.......... cut end of nerve fiber (axon)?
Physiology + সরল ও দ্বিপদী সমীকরণ এবং অস.exp:
Wallerian degeneration occurs in the distal segment of a severed or severely injured axon, i.e., the portion distal to the site of injury. Because this segment is separated from the neuron's cell body, the axon and its myelin sheath undergo degeneration.

The proximal segment may undergo limited degeneration initially, but it can survive because it remains connected to the cell body.

Other options:

  • Proximal: Usually remains viable and may undergo regenerative changes.

  • Middle: Not a standard anatomical division used for Wallerian degeneration.

  • Near to middle: Not applicable.

High-yield Neurophysiology recall:
Axonal injury → distal segment → Wallerian degeneration.

Exam pearl:
Wallerian degeneration = degeneration of the distal axon after nerve injury.

Physiology + সরল ও দ্বিপদী সমীকরণ এবং অস.question: ৬) Which of the following is not a criteria of Axon?
Physiology + সরল ও দ্বিপদী সমীকরণ এবং অস.exp:
Nissl granules (Nissl bodies) are present in the cell body and dendrites, but they are absent from the axon and axon hillock. Therefore, their presence is not a characteristic of an axon.

Other options:

  • Single in number: A neuron generally has a single axon.

  • No branching: Classically described as an axon being unbranched near its origin, although axon collaterals can occur.

  • Arises from axon hillock: Correct; the axon originates from the axon hillock/initial segment.

High-yield Neuroanatomy recall:
Nissl bodies → soma + dendrites; absent in axon and axon hillock.

Exam pearl:
No Nissl substance in the axon hillock = key identifying feature.

Physiology + সরল ও দ্বিপদী সমীকরণ এবং অস.question: ৭) Which neurotransmitter acts rapidly?
Physiology + সরল ও দ্বিপদী সমীকরণ এবং অস.exp:
Dopamine is a rapid-acting neurotransmitter in the CNS. It is released from presynaptic neurons and acts on dopamine receptors to transmit signals rapidly across synapses.

The other listed substances—vasopressin, insulin, and growth hormone—are primarily hormones, producing slower, longer-lasting effects through endocrine signaling.

Other options:

  • Vasopressin: Peptide hormone; acts mainly through endocrine signaling.

  • Insulin: Peptide hormone regulating glucose metabolism.

  • Growth hormone: Peptide hormone involved in growth and metabolism.

High-yield Neurotransmitter recall:
Classical fast neurotransmitters include glutamate, GABA, acetylcholine, and dopamine; neuropeptides generally act more slowly and modulatory.

Exam pearl:
Dopamine is a neurotransmitter; vasopressin, insulin, and GH are hormones.

Physiology + সরল ও দ্বিপদী সমীকরণ এবং অস.question: ৮) All of the following chemical mediators are neurotransmitter except..?
Physiology + সরল ও দ্বিপদী সমীকরণ এবং অস.exp:
Amphetamine is a psychoactive drug/stimulant, not a neurotransmitter. It increases the release and reduces the reuptake of monoamines such as dopamine and norepinephrine.

Other options:

  • ACh (acetylcholine): A major neurotransmitter in the CNS and peripheral nervous system.

  • Histamine: Acts as a neurotransmitter in the CNS, particularly from neurons in the hypothalamus.

  • Dopamine: A major catecholamine neurotransmitter involved in movement, reward, motivation, and endocrine regulation.

High-yield Neurotransmitter recall:
ACh, dopamine, histamine → neurotransmitters
Amphetamine → drug that modifies neurotransmitter activity

Exam pearl:
Amphetamine is not a neurotransmitter; it enhances monoaminergic transmission.

Physiology + সরল ও দ্বিপদী সমীকরণ এবং অস.question: ৯) Which sensation is transmitted through dorsal column of spinal cord?
Physiology + সরল ও দ্বিপদী সমীকরণ এবং অস.exp:
The dorsal column–medial lemniscus pathway carries fine/discriminative touch, vibration, conscious proprioception, and pressure. The dorsal columns consist mainly of the fasciculus gracilis and fasciculus cuneatus.

Other options:

  • Pain: Mainly carried by the spinothalamic tract.

  • Touch: Can be carried by both pathways, but fine/discriminative touch is specifically carried by the dorsal column.

  • Temperature: Mainly carried by the spinothalamic tract.

High-yield Dorsal column recall:
Dorsal column → vibration + fine touch + proprioception.

Exam pearl:
Vibration sense = dorsal column–medial lemniscus pathway.

Physiology + সরল ও দ্বিপদী সমীকরণ এবং অস.question: ১০) Which one is responsible for formation of myelin sheath in CNS?
Physiology + সরল ও দ্বিপদী সমীকরণ এবং অস.exp:
In the CNS, myelin sheath is formed by oligodendrocytes. A single oligodendrocyte can myelinate segments of multiple axons.

Other options:

  • Astrocyte: Provides structural, metabolic, and supportive functions; does not form myelin.

  • Ependymal cell: Lines the ventricles and central canal and is associated with CSF production/circulation.

  • Schwann cell: Forms myelin in the PNS, not CNS.

High-yield Neuroanatomy recall:
CNS → Oligodendrocyte
PNS → Schwann cell

Exam pearl:
Oligodendrocyte = CNS myelin; Schwann cell = PNS myelin.

Physiology + সরল ও দ্বিপদী সমীকরণ এবং অস.question: ১১) Which one is the features of LMNL?
Physiology + সরল ও দ্বিপদী সমীকরণ এবং অস.exp:
Lower motor neuron lesion (LMNL) causes damage to the anterior horn cell, motor root, or peripheral motor nerve. A characteristic feature is fasciculation—visible, spontaneous twitching of individual muscle fibers due to instability of the denervated motor unit.

Typical features of LMNL include:

  • Decreased muscle tone (flaccidity)

  • Decreased or absent deep tendon reflexes

  • Muscle wasting/atrophy

  • Fasciculations

Other options:

  • Increased tone: Characteristic of an UMN lesion.

  • Increased jerk: UMN lesion typically causes brisk/increased reflexes.

  • Spasticity: Characteristic of an UMN lesion.

High-yield LMN vs UMN recall:

Feature LMN lesion UMN lesion
Tone Decreased Increased
Reflexes Decreased/absent Increased
Atrophy Marked Mild/disuse
Fasciculation Present Absent
Plantar response Flexor/absent Extensor (Babinski)

Exam pearl:
Fasciculation + wasting + hyporeflexia + hypotonia = LMN lesion.

Physiology + সরল ও দ্বিপদী সমীকরণ এবং অস.question: ১২) Speed of conduction of a nerve fiber is inversely proportional to which of the following?
Physiology + সরল ও দ্বিপদী সমীকরণ এবং অস.exp:
The conduction velocity of a nerve fiber is affected by several factors. It increases with fiber diameter and temperature, while mechanical pressure on a nerve can reduce conduction velocity by compressing the nerve and impairing axonal membrane function.

Other options:

  • Thickness of nerve fiber: Conduction velocity is directly proportional to fiber diameter; thicker fibers conduct faster.

  • Temperature: Within physiological limits, increased temperature generally increases conduction velocity.

  • pH: Abnormal pH can affect nerve conduction, but it is not the standard inverse relationship tested here.

High-yield Neurophysiology recall:
Conduction velocity ↑ with: larger diameter, myelination, and physiological warming.
Conduction velocity ↓ with: compression, demyelination, and cooling.

Exam pearl:
Thicker + myelinated nerve → faster conduction; mechanical pressure → slower conduction.

Physiology + সরল ও দ্বিপদী সমীকরণ এবং অস.question: ১৩) Which of the following is a excitatory neurotransmitter?
Physiology + সরল ও দ্বিপদী সমীকরণ এবং অস.exp:
Glutamate is the principal excitatory neurotransmitter in the CNS. It produces excitatory postsynaptic potentials mainly through AMPA and NMDA receptors.

Other options:

  • Glycine: Mainly an inhibitory neurotransmitter, especially in the spinal cord and brainstem.

  • Serotonin: Primarily a neuromodulator; its effect can be excitatory or inhibitory depending on the receptor.

  • Alanine: An amino acid but not a major neurotransmitter in the CNS.

High-yield Neurotransmitter recall:
Main excitatory neurotransmitter → Glutamate
Main inhibitory neurotransmitters → GABA (brain) and glycine (spinal cord)

Exam pearl:
Glutamate = major excitatory neurotransmitter of the CNS.

Physiology + সরল ও দ্বিপদী সমীকরণ এবং অস.question: ১৪) Which one is not a properties of synapse??
Physiology + সরল ও দ্বিপদী সমীকরণ এবং অস.exp:
Synaptic stimulation is not considered a standard property of synapses. Synapses have characteristic physiological properties such as synaptic delay, synaptic response, and synaptic inhibition.

A synapse is the functional junction where a signal is transmitted from one neuron to another neuron or an effector cell.

Other options:

  • Synaptic delay: Present because neurotransmitter release, diffusion, and receptor activation take a finite amount of time.

  • Synaptic response: A postsynaptic response occurs following neurotransmitter release.

  • Synaptic inhibition: A well-established synaptic function, producing inhibitory postsynaptic potentials (IPSPs).

High-yield Synapse recall:
Important properties include one-way conduction, synaptic delay, summation, facilitation, inhibition, fatigue, and plasticity.

Exam pearl:
Synaptic stimulation is not a standard physiological property of a synapse.

Physiology + সরল ও দ্বিপদী সমীকরণ এবং অস.question: ১৫) According to function, synapse are of ... types?
Physiology + সরল ও দ্বিপদী সমীকরণ এবং অস.exp:
According to function, synapses are classically divided into 2 types:

  1. Excitatory synapse — increases the likelihood of an action potential in the postsynaptic neuron.

  2. Inhibitory synapse — decreases the likelihood of an action potential in the postsynaptic neuron.

Other options:

  • 3, 4, 5: Not the standard functional classification of synapses.

High-yield Synapse recall:
Functional classification → excitatory + inhibitory = 2 types.

Exam pearl:
Synapse by function = 2 types: excitatory and inhibitory.

Physiology + সরল ও দ্বিপদী সমীকরণ এবং অস.question: ১৬) Which one is a criteria of neurotransmitter?
Physiology + সরল ও দ্বিপদী সমীকরণ এবং অস.option1: It must be found in a neuron
Physiology + সরল ও দ্বিপদী সমীকরণ এবং অস.option2: It must be produced by a neuron
Physiology + সরল ও দ্বিপদী সমীকরণ এবং অস.option3: It must be released by a neuron
Physiology + সরল ও দ্বিপদী সমীকরণ এবং অস.exp:
For a substance to be considered a neurotransmitter, it should fulfill several criteria:

  • It is present in the presynaptic neuron.

  • It is synthesized/produced by the neuron.

  • It is released from the neuron in response to appropriate stimulation, typically with Ca²⁺-dependent exocytosis.

  • It acts on specific receptors on the postsynaptic cell and produces a physiological response.

Therefore, all three statements are accepted as criteria in standard physiology.

Other options:

  • It must be found in a neuron: Correct.

  • It must be produced by a neuron: Correct.

  • It must be released by a neuron: Correct.

High-yield Neurotransmitter recall:
Synthesized/present → stored → released → acts on specific receptor → produces response.

Exam pearl:
Neurotransmitter criteria given individually here are all correct → All.

Physiology + সরল ও দ্বিপদী সমীকরণ এবং অস.question: ১৭) Site of secretion of Aspartate are following, except..?
Physiology + সরল ও দ্বিপদী সমীকরণ এবং অস.exp:
Aspartate is an excitatory amino-acid neurotransmitter found in several regions of the CNS. It is particularly associated with the cerebellum, spinal cord, and retina. The brainstem is not considered a major/classical site of aspartate secretion in standard physiology MCQ classifications.

Other options:

  • Cerebellum: Contains aspartate as an excitatory amino-acid neurotransmitter.

  • Spinal cord: Aspartate is present and can participate in excitatory neurotransmission.

  • Retina: Aspartate is found in retinal neurons and participates in excitatory signaling.

High-yield Neurotransmitter recall:
Aspartate → cerebellum + spinal cord + retina (classically listed sites).

Exam pearl:
For this MCQ: Aspartate secretion—think cerebellum, spinal cord, retina; exception = brainstem.

Physiology + সরল ও দ্বিপদী সমীকরণ এবং অস.question: ১৮) Each bundle of nerve fibers is called......?
Physiology + সরল ও দ্বিপদী সমীকরণ এবং অস.exp:
A fasciculus (fascicle) is a bundle of nerve fibers (axons) within a peripheral nerve.

The connective tissue coverings are arranged as:

  • Endoneurium: Surrounds each individual nerve fiber.

  • Perineurium: Surrounds each fasciculus.

  • Epineurium: Surrounds the entire nerve.

Other options:

  • Epineurium: Covers the whole peripheral nerve.

  • Endoneurium: Covers individual axons/nerve fibers.

  • Perineurium: Covers a fasciculus, but is not the name of the bundle itself.

High-yield Peripheral nerve recall:
Nerve fiber → Endoneurium → Fasciculus → Perineurium → Whole nerve → Epineurium

Exam pearl:
Bundle of nerve fibers = fasciculus; covering of fasciculus = perineurium.

Physiology + সরল ও দ্বিপদী সমীকরণ এবং অস.question: ১৯) Myelin sheath is responsible for.........color of nerve fibers?
Physiology + সরল ও দ্বিপদী সমীকরণ এবং অস.exp:
The myelin sheath is rich in lipids, which gives myelinated nerve fibers a white appearance. This is why regions of the CNS containing many myelinated axons are called white matter.

Other options:

  • Yellow: Not the characteristic color produced by myelin.

  • Blue: Not associated with myelin coloration.

  • Red: Not associated with myelin.

High-yield Neuroanatomy recall:
Myelin-rich tissue → white matter
Neuron cell bodies, dendrites, and unmyelinated fibers → gray matter

Exam pearl:
Myelin sheath = lipid-rich → white color → white matter.

Physiology + সরল ও দ্বিপদী সমীকরণ এবং অস.question: ২০) Meissner's corpuscles is a receptor for which of the following sensation?
Physiology + সরল ও দ্বিপদী সমীকরণ এবং অস.exp:
Meissner’s corpuscles are specialized mechanoreceptors located mainly in the dermal papillae of glabrous skin (e.g., fingertips, palms, soles). They are responsible for detecting fine/light touch, particularly low-frequency vibration and rapidly changing tactile stimuli.

Other options:

  • Pain: Mainly detected by free nerve endings (nociceptors).

  • Heat: Detected mainly by free nerve endings (thermoreceptors).

  • Cold: Detected mainly by free nerve endings (thermoreceptors).

High-yield Sensory receptor recall:

  • Meissner corpuscle → fine/light touch

  • Pacinian corpuscle → deep pressure + high-frequency vibration

  • Merkel discs → sustained pressure/fine touch

  • Ruffini endings → skin stretch

  • Free nerve endings → pain + temperature

Exam pearl:
Meissner = light touch; Pacinian = vibration/deep pressure.
